answers.answer: Assuming A, B, C, D lie on the circle (the figure is not available, so this is assumed): $\angle B$ and $\angle C$ are inscribed angles subtended by the same arc $AD$, so $m(\angle B)=m(\angle C)$, i.e. $m(\angle ABD)... $ in $\triangle EBC$, $m(\angle B)=m(\angle C)$. Hence $\triangle EBC$ is isosceles and $EB=EC$.

Since chords $AD=BE$ in the same circle, their arcs are equal, so the inscribed angles $\angle ABD$ and $\angle BAE$ are equal. Hence in $\triangle CAB$, $m(\angle CAB)=m(\angle CBA)$, so $CA=CB$. Then $CD=CA-AD$ and $CE=CB-BE$ with $AD=BE$, so $CD=CE$.
